topic: How does regenerative payload placement affect feeder link interface choices and network resource management?
response: Regenerative payload placement affects feeder link interface choices and network resource management by enabling the reuse of feeder link bandwidth through geographical displacement of gateways. This approach requires additional gateways in standby or spare capacity reserved at active gateways to cope with heavy rain fades and high-frequency band limitations.
reference_context: The context mentions that gateways have to be displaced geographically to allow the reuse of feeder link bandwidth, and transmit diversity techniques are needed to cope with heavy rain fades in frequency bands up to 5 GHz.
